content_html:
Sour odor, clumping, and texture changes can indicate spoilage, but safety should not be judged by the senses alone. Time out of refrigeration, temperature, and how long the container has been open matter more.

Start with temperature history

If milk spent too long at room temperature, it may be unsafe even if it still smells normal. Use time-and-temperature rules to make the decision.

Use texture and odor as quality clues

Unusual separation, clumps, or a clearly sour smell are reasons to discard it. Do not taste questionable milk to confirm.

The printed date is not the whole story

Once opened, handling and temperature matter greatly. Follow manufacturer guidance and keep the refrigerator at a safe temperature.

UHT is different before opening, not after

Ultra-high-temperature (UHT) milk can be shelf-stable while unopened when labeled that way. After opening, refrigerate it according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
